tasks.short: Monitor weather effects on concrete curing

steps.what: Monitor wind, heat and cold effects on concrete curing throughout the process

tasks.design: Retain on-site observation of concrete and weather effects, using the curing specification in {DOCS}. A weather display alone does not replace checking actual surface and curing conditions, so no new software saving is claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forecast conditions do not fully describe the curing state of a particular pour.
tasks.enabler_now: No new digital capability establishes a safe reduction in direct observation for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Wind exposure, local shade, surface drying and concrete condition interact over time.
tasks.human_edge: The finisher connects visible curing changes to local conditions and flags a need for action.
tasks.altitude: Observation responsibility and escalation remain unchanged.

reach.task: Agree a response to weather-related curing concerns
reach.learn: Project curing requirements and limits of the finisher's authority

evidence.claim: Local curing observations cannot be replaced by a generic weather view in this task-specific assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring conditions and raising concerns, not application of curing treatments, preparation of progress reports or structural acceptance.
The finisher produces observations by inspecting concrete and local conditions in s1; all time stays counted. No ready sensor-derived curing status or structured exposure flag is assumed.
Existing native weather or project information may be consulted but its runtime is not human saving. No sensor deployment or automated engineering decision is proposed.
No tool or process change means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Existing local measurements and inspection frequency
research_questions: Which curing observations actually require direct inspection under the site's method?

already_counted.description: Direct monitoring, interpretation and raising concerns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; direct monitoring remains. Gross and net saving zero with no added upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Position concrete truck and direct chute flow

steps.what: Signal truck driver to position truck for pouring concrete
Move chute to direct concrete onto forms while coordinating with the driver

tasks.design: Keep truck signalling and chute handling with the finisher at the pour, informed by the existing site method in {DOCS}. No screen-based instruction replaces direct sight of the vehicle, people and flowing concrete.
tasks.previous_blocker: Positioning and placement require continuous physical coordination in a changing work area.
tasks.enabler_now: No software-only change removes signalling or chute handling.
tasks.still_hard: Obstructions, people near the truck and changing flow require immediate responses.
tasks.human_edge: The finisher maintains shared understanding with the driver and adjusts placement on site.
tasks.altitude: The finisher continues to coordinate truck position and concrete placement.

reach.task: Confirm positioning and flow signals before the pour

evidence.claim: Truck signalling and chute movement remain direct physical coordination in this assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is the finisher's signalling and chute movement. Driver labour, truck travel and other crew placement work are excluded and receive no saving.
The finisher checks actual access and form position in s1 and s2, with all time retained. No structured clear-route or safe-position flag is assumed.
The existing site method is unchanged; there is no new controller, robotics or remote vehicle operation.
No process or system is changed, so recurring upkeep is zero.
research_questions: How are stop signals and visibility maintained during actual pours?

already_counted.description: Physical chute movement and flow coordination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+65=100; no finisher work is removed. Gross and net zero with zero upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct concrete casting and supervise spreading crews

steps.what: Direct concrete casting and supervise laborers spreading it with shovels or tools

tasks.design: Retain on-site direction of casting and spreading, with the pour plan available in {DOCS}. A digital task list does not replace observation of placement, crew actions and concrete behaviour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Casting progresses continuously and the crew must respond to actual placement conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability establishes a reduction in the direct supervision duty.
tasks.still_hard: Timing, coverage, obstructions and emerging defects demand practical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The finisher sees work quality as it develops and gives immediate, understandable direction.
tasks.altitude: Supervision and placement responsibility remain with the finisher.

reach.task: Resolve pour-plan conflicts or material problems reported during casting
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds and project placement requirements

evidence.claim: Direct concrete casting supervision remains situated human work; no new automation saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the finisher's direct casting and spreading supervision, not crew labour, truck signalling or later reporting. Adjacent tasks must not duplicate the same direction time in a role roll-up.
The finisher gathers placement progress and crew observations directly in s1 with all time counted. No structured work-complete or quality status is assumed for free.
Use existing plans and native project references as they stand; no new digital capture or automated crew allocation is introduced.
There is no new tool or upkeep, so incremental hours are zero.
research_questions: Which casting decisions must the finisher make as placement conditions change?

already_counted.description: Live casting direction and spreading supervision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; supervision time stays intact. Gross and net saving zero with no added upkeep.

role.altitude: Concrete observation, signalling, placement and supervision remain physical responsibilities.
reach: Coordinate directly with drivers and placing crews
Escalate curing and placement concerns to site supervisors
role.ambitious_version: A finisher who directs and observes the pour reliably; no software-driven expansion is claimed for these tasks.
